lines.text: Missing side in a right-angled triangle, two sides known → Pythagoras: add the squares for the hypotenuse, subtract for a shorter side ({{lesson:6.1}})
Right-angled triangle, an angle and one side known, another side wanted → label opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse from the angle, then use $\sin$, $\cos$ or $\tan$ (SOH CAH TOA) ({{lesson:6.2}})
Missing angle in a right-angled triangle, two sides known → $\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$ or $\tan^{-1}$ in degree mode, to 1 d.p. ({{lesson:6.2}})
Bearings, or a right angle hidden in a bigger shape → draw one right-angled triangle at a time and keep full values between steps ({{lesson:6.2}})
Angle of elevation or depression → measure it from the horizontal; the depression from the top equals the elevation from the bottom, so use it inside the right-angled triangle ({{lesson:6.2}})
Shortest distance from a point to a line → the perpendicular distance, at right angles to the line ({{lesson:6.2}})
No calculator, angle of $30^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ or $60^{\circ}$ → exact values from half a square or half an equilateral triangle ({{lesson:6.3}})

Solve $\sin x = k$, $\cos x = k$ or $\tan x = k$ for $0^{\circ} \leqslant x \leqslant 360^{\circ}$ → find one angle with the minus sign ignored, then sketch the graph and the line $y = k$: every crossing in the range is an answer ({{lesson:6.4}})
Triangle with no right angle, a side and the angle across from it known → sine rule; for an angle, also try $180^{\circ} - x$ and keep it if it fits with the other angles ({{lesson:6.5}})
Triangle with no right angle, two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides → cosine rule ({{lesson:6.5}})
Area of a triangle from two sides and the angle between them → $\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ ({{lesson:6.5}})

Length or angle inside a cuboid or pyramid → draw the hidden right-angled triangle flat; space diagonal $d^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}$; for a line and a plane, use the angle between the line and its projection ({{lesson:6.6}})
